svg.title: Countably generated measurable isotropy need not admit a compatible locally compact group topology
svg.desc: A choice construction gives a subgroup of the real line and its disjoint coset meeting every perfect set. The trace Lebesgue measure gives a proper transverse regular representation. A hypothesized compatible locally compact topology would force countable compact neighborhoods, then discreteness, contradicting the size of its Borel algebra.

text.tspan: Countable generation does not supply the isotropy topology
A complete counterexample at the supplied source’s measurable scope
1. A subgroup selected through all perfect sets (Theorem 1.2)
κ = |ℝ|; enumerate every nonempty perfect Pα, α < κ.
Choose hα ∈ Pα outside spanℚ({1} ∪ {hβ : β < α}).
Excluded span has size < κ.
Every perfect Pα has size κ.
H = spanℚ{hα}; |H| = κ; 1 ∉ H.
H and H + 1 are disjoint.
Every perfect P meets both H and H + 1. Neither coset contains a perfect set.
This is a choice construction, not a membership plot of H.
2. All measurable and representation hypotheses hold
Σ = {B ∩ H : B Borel in ℝ}; countably generated and point-separating.
μ(B ∩ H) = λ(B); well-defined, σ-finite, nonzero and translation-invariant.
One-unit groupoid; faithful transverse function ν = μ.
Aₙ = H ∩ [−n,n]; μ(Aₙ − h) = 2n for every h ∈ H.
J : L²(ℝ,λ) → L²(H,μ) is unitary; U(h)J = J λℝ(h).
∫H |⟨Ja,U(h)Jξ⟩|² dμ(h) ≤ ‖ξ‖₁² ‖a‖₂², ξ ∈ Cc(ℝ).
3. A compatible locally compact topology would contradict cardinality
Assume Bor(H,τ) = Σ, τ locally compact.
Inclusion i : H → ℝ is Borel.
Baire/Pettis argument ⇒ i is continuous.
Compact neighborhood K maps into H.
i(K) compact in ℝ; no perfect subset.
Hence K is countable.
A countable nonempty open V ⊂ K is locally compact and Baire.
An isolated point must exist ⇒ translations make τ discrete.
Then Bor(H,τ) = 𝒫(H).
But |Σ| ≤ κ < 2^κ = |𝒫(H)|. Contradiction.
Theorem 4.2; exact source comparison: supplied Connes PDF 8–9 and Proposition 15, PDF 30–31.
The general nontrivial-isotropy commutant/disintegration proof remains a separate open requirement.
